before.problem:
Suppose we wish to approximate the solution to an initial value problem using the following numerical method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =({x}^{2}+y)\cdot Δx \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy\end{aligned}
$$

If the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)={x}^{3},$ find an expression for the local truncation error for the step from $x$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx.$

Suppose we wish to approximate the solution to an initial value problem using the following numerical method: Δy=(x2+y)⋅Δxynew=y+Δy If the exact solution is yexact(x)=x3, find an expression for the local truncation error for the step from x to xnew=x+Δx.

a
(2x3−x2)Δx+x(Δx)2+(Δx)3
b
(x2−x3)Δx+2x(Δx)2+x(Δx)3
c
(x3−2x2)Δx+3x(Δx)2+(Δx)3
d
(2x2−x3)Δx+3x(Δx)2+(Δx)3
e
(x2−2x3)Δx+3x(Δx)2+4x(Δx)3
Submit

decision.explanation: Starting from the exact value y=x^3, the method gives y_new=x^3+(x^2+x^3)Δx. The local truncation error is the exact next value minus this approximation: (x+Δx)^3−[x^3+(x^2+x^3)Δx]=(2x^2−x^3)Δx+3x(Δx)^2+(Δx)^3.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Suppose we wish to approximate the solution to an initial value problem using the following numerical method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =({x}^{2}+y)\cdot Δx \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy\end{aligned}
$$

If the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)={x}^{3},$ find an expression for the local truncation error for the step from $x$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx.$
after.worked_solution:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a *single step* of a numerical method, when the step begins from an *exact value*. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that the exact solution of the initial value problem is $y(x)={x}^{3}.$ Now, let's find the $y$-increment given by the numerical method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =({x}^{2}+{y}_{\text{exact}}(x))\cdot Δx \\  & =({x}^{2}+{x}^{3})\cdot Δx.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the exact value at ${x}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(x+Δx) \\  & =(x+Δx)^{3} \\  & ={x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}\cdot Δx+3x\cdot (Δx)^{2}+(Δx)^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the LTE for step $n$ starting at $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & =[{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}\cdot Δx+3x\cdot (Δx)^{2}+(Δx)^{3}]-[{x}^{3}+({x}^{2}+{x}^{3})\cdot Δx] \\  & ={x}^{3}-{x}^{3}+(3{x}^{2}-({x}^{2}+{x}^{3}))\cdot Δx+3x\cdot (Δx)^{2}+(Δx)^{3} \\  & =(2{x}^{2}-{x}^{3})Δx+3x(Δx)^{2}+(Δx)^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

a
(2x3−x2)Δx+x(Δx)2+(Δx)3
b
(x2−x3)Δx+2x(Δx)2+x(Δx)3
c
(x3−2x2)Δx+3x(Δx)2+(Δx)3
d
(2x2−x3)Δx+3x(Δx)2+(Δx)3
e
(x2−2x3)Δx+3x(Δx)2+4x(Δx)3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a single step of a numerical method, when the step begins from an exact value. The LTE of a numerical method at step n from x with exact value yexact(x) to xnew=x+Δx is τn=yexact(xnew)−ynew=yexact(xnew)−(yexact(x)+Δy).

We're given that the exact solution of the initial value problem is y(x)=x3. Now, let's find the y-increment given by the numerical method:

Δy=(x2+yexact(x))⋅Δx=(x2+x3)⋅Δx.

Next, we compute the exact value at xnew:

yexact(xnew)=yexact(x+Δx)=(x+Δx)3=x3+3x2⋅Δx+3x⋅(Δx)2+(Δx)3

Finally, we calculate the LTE for step n starting at x:

τn=yexact(xnew)−ynew=[x3+3x2⋅Δx+3x⋅(Δx)2+(Δx)3]−[x3+(x2+x3)⋅Δx]=x3−x3+(3x2−(x2+x3))⋅Δx+3x⋅(Δx)2+(Δx)3=(2x2−x3)Δx+3x(Δx)2+(Δx)3

content.problem:
Suppose we wish to approximate the solution to an initial value problem using the following numerical method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =({x}^{2}+y)\cdot Δx \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy\end{aligned}
$$

If the exact solution is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)={x}^{3},$ find an expression for the local truncation error for the step from $x$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx.$
content.worked_solution:
The local truncation error (LTE) is the error made in a *single step* of a numerical method, when the step begins from an *exact value*. The LTE of a numerical method at step $n$ from $x$ with exact value ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)$ to ${x}_{\text{new}}=x+Δx$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that the exact solution of the initial value problem is $y(x)={x}^{3}.$ Now, let's find the $y$-increment given by the numerical method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =({x}^{2}+{y}_{\text{exact}}(x))\cdot Δx \\  & =({x}^{2}+{x}^{3})\cdot Δx.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the exact value at ${x}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}}) & ={y}_{\text{exact}}(x+Δx) \\  & =(x+Δx)^{3} \\  & ={x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}\cdot Δx+3x\cdot (Δx)^{2}+(Δx)^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{τ}_{n} & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}} \\  & ={y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}})-({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δy).\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that the exact solution of the initial value problem is ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)=3{x}^{2}+5x.$ Now, let's find the $y$-increment given by the numerical method.

First, the slope at a step starting at $x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(x)=(3{x}^{2}+5x)^{′}=6x+5.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the increment given by the numerical method is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}_{\text{exact}}^{′}(x)\cdot Δx \\  & =(6x+5)\cdot Δx.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the exact value at ${x}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{exact}}({x}_{\text{new}}) & =({y}_{\text{exact}}(x)+Δx) \\  & =3(x+Δx)^{2}+5(x+Δx) \\  & =3({x}^{2}+2x\cdot Δx+(Δx)^{2})+5x+5\cdot Δx \\  & =3{x}^{2}+6x\cdot Δx+3\cdot (Δx)^{2}+5x+5\cdot Δx \\  & =3{x}^{2}+(6x+5)\cdot Δx+3\cdot (Δx)^{2}+5x\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
